subject: Phased VPC lift-and-guard ops plan ahead of renewal
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@medsyshealth.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@medsyshealth.com
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Scaling needs and isolation ask ahead of contract renewal

Hi Irene —

Thanks for taking the time last week. MedSys is nearing our third-year renewal window and we
are looking to both expand capacity and separate analytics workloads into an isolated VPC for
PHI processing. High level asks: additional two inference clusters (GPU-heavy), a standby
failover cluster in us-west for DR, and a stricter network segregation policy for analytics.

I attached a filled capacity workbook that shows our peak token/sec and expected growth.
Can you confirm if Redwood can support a canary cutover approach (stage analytics into the
new VPC, validate KV cache behavior, then re-point traffic)? Also need a rough price delta and
whether the renewal term can be adjusted to 36 months to smooth costs.

Appreciate a proposed timeline so we can align procurement.

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform, MedSys Health
[Attachment: medsys_capacity_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@medsyshealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Scaling needs and isolation ask ahead of contract renewal

Alex —

Thanks for the clear workbook. Short answers up front: yes, we can do staged canary cutovers and
we can provision an isolated analytics VPC with dedicated clusters + standby failover.
Term flexibility is possible (36 months) — finance will need the final capacity profile.

I looped in Karthik (solutions) for the technical cutover plan and Dev (account) for the
commercial/contract side. Preliminary timeline (ballpark):
- Week 1–2: sizing and template SOW (we draft)
- Week 3: provisioning of isolated VPC + one cluster seed
- Week 4–6: canary cutover & validation (analytics workload)
- Week 7: full traffic migration and failover exercises

Can Karthik propose a node layout and validation checklist? Dev — once we have the SOW
I can share a terms summary to present to procurement.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_sow_placeholder.docx (draft placeholder)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@medsyshealth.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-17T14:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Scaling needs and isolation ask ahead of contract renewal

Alex / Irene —

Reviewed the workbook. Suggestion for a conservative initial layout to avoid noisy rollbacks: 
- Analytics VPC (isolated): 2x rtx-8k clusters (quantized runtime for inference analytics),
  pinned model variants for PHI workloads, strict egress rules.
- Primary inference fleet: add 2 x burst-capacity clusters (auto-burst up to 20% for peaks).
- Standby failover: 1 small cluster in us-west with warm KV-cache snapshot replication.

Validation checklist for canary cutover (high level):
1) KV cache consistency test with sampled sessions
2) End-to-end latency SLO check (p95 <= target)
3) Privileged endpoint isolation verification (no cross-VPC access)
4) DR failover exercise using traffic shadowing

Ops notes: We may recommend enabling prefix-KV caching for analytics to reduce token cost;
this impacts cache warm-up plan during the canary window. I will draft a detailed node map
and checklist in a follow-up.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: procurement@medsyshealth.com <procurement@medsyshealth.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@medsyshealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Scaling needs and isolation ask ahead of contract renewal

Irene / Dev —

Procurement here. A few procurement-specific asks before we can sign off on a 36-month term: 
1) Need a draft SOW with milestone-based acceptance criteria.
2) Can you provide SOC2 evidence and an audit window for VPC isolation testing?
3) Are there price breakpoints for multi-year commitment (36 vs 24 months)?

We received the capacity workbook and the numbers look reasonable. Please include a separate
line for one-time provisioning vs recurring monthly commit. If you can get a DocuSign for the
SOW + order form, we can queue it in our signature cycle (procurement SLA ~ 7 business days).

Thanks — we prefer consolidated docs to send to legal.

Procurement Team
MedSys Health
[Attachment: security-evidence-package.zip (archive)]
